observations: Photo 0 shows two dry irons: one cream-colored and one pink, both with 'Panasonic' branding and labels for fabric types (Acrylic, Nylon, Polyester). The irons are visibly worn with scuffs and dirt. The pink iron has 'MBA' written on it.
Photo 1 shows a silver and pink dry iron with a coiled cord and a white plug labeled 'MAY'. The soleplate is metallic and appears clean. The brand 'MAY' is visible on the plug.

Photo 2 shows a black and silver dry iron with a coiled cord and a white plug. The brand 'Good' is visible on a sticker. The soleplate is metallic and appears clean. The handle has a dial and a small orange button.
All three photos show dry irons with coiled cords and plugs, consistent with the seller's description of 'Professional dry pressing iron' and 'Heavy-duty dry iron'.
The irons appear to be used, with visible wear and dirt, especially on the pink iron and the black iron in photo 2.

claims.evidence: All three photos show dry irons with labels for fabric types (Acrylic, Nylon, Polyester) and coiled cords, consistent with professional use.
The irons appear to be heavy-duty based on size and design, but no proof of durability or build quality is visible. The soleplates are metallic and appear thick, but this is subjective.
All three photos show electric irons with coiled cords and plugs, consistent with electric dry irons.

risks.proof: Close-up photos of the handle, dial, and cord for signs of damage or wear.

response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
